data.title: Bank of Nassau 1982 Chief Economist Win Thin Says August U.S. CPI Does Not Meet Warsh's 2% Inflation Standard
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Bank of Nassau 1982 Chief Economist Win Thin said the August U.S. CPI data does not seem to meet the standard set by Fed Governor Kevin Warsh for returning inflation to 2%, and he expects the Federal Reserve to raise rates next week as markets have almost fully priced in a rate hike.

data.title: BMO Capital Markets' Ian Lyngen: August CPI Clears Path for Fed Rate Hike Next Week
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, BMO Capital Markets U.S. rates strategy head Ian Lyngen said the August U.S. CPI inflation report cleared the path for an FOMC rate hike next week, and he expects at least one more 25-basis-point hike before year-end. Short-dated bonds weakened, while longer-duration bonds rose.

data.title: The Smarter Web Company Considers Preferred Share Offering on London Stock Exchange
data.description:
The Smarter Web Company is considering issuing preferred shares under the reserved code MORE for trading on the London Stock Exchange main market. The company plans to hold an extraordinary general meeting on September 28 to seek approval for the related authorization matters. According to Foresight News, the preferred shares would offer cumulative variable-rate weekly preferred dividends and liquidation preference, but no voting rights.

The company plans to raise 15 million to 25 million pounds, with dividend payments expected to come from operating cash flow, its Bitcoin treasury, and capital market fundraising. Chief Executive Officer Andrew Webley said that, if approved, it would be the first perpetual preferred share issued by a UK-listed company with a Bitcoin treasury strategy and listed on the London Stock Exchange main market.

data.title: India's Foreign Ministry: Modi Stresses Need for Lasting Peace and Stability in the Region
data.description: According to Jin10, India's Foreign Ministry said that during a meeting with Iranian President Pezeshkian, Indian Prime Minister Modi emphasized the importance of continued efforts to ensure lasting peace and stability in the region.

data.title: SpaceX Faces Musk’s Trade-Off Between Starship, AI and Starlink
data.description:
Elon Musk is weighing whether SpaceX should focus on cash-generating satellite launches or on sending humans into deep space, according to Bloomberg.

The company’s strategy centers on balancing Starship, artificial intelligence ambitions and Starlink, while the payoff remains uncertain.

data.title: The Smarter Web Company Plans UK’s First Bitcoin-Backed Preferred Share Offering
data.description: The Smarter Web Company said it plans to launch the UK’s first preferred share backed by Bitcoin, subject to shareholder approval. According to Odaily, the company expects to raise $20 million to $34 million through a potential IPO to buy more Bitcoin and acquire operating businesses that generate cash flow.

data.title: Bitcoin News | Bitcoin Rebounds $3,255 From $76,046 Low to Clear $79,000 After the CPI Print
data.description: Bitcoin rebounded by more than $3,000 following the CPI release, breaking through $79,000 to trade at $79,301 — a 24-hour gain of 2.68%.It had briefly dipped to $76,046 before the reversal, a move of $3,255 from low to current price.The Rally Came Despite a Hot Core PrintThe direction is counterintuitive on the data alone.Core CPI rose 0.3% in August against 0.2% expected — the single figure in the release that missed, and the one that annualizes to roughly 3.7%. Headline came in at 0.4% monthly and 3.4% annually, both in line, with core at 2.4% year-over-year, also in line.Three readings matched and one came in hot. A market that spent Thursday selling off through a soft core PPI print might reasonably have sold this harder.Resolved Uncertainty Rather Than Better NewsThe most defensible explanation is that the print collapsed a disagreement rather than delivering good news.Hike odds had been split widely across venues before the release — 76% on CME FedWatch, roughly two-thirds per QCP, and 61% on Polymarket. A 15-point spread on a binary event three business days out indicated genuine uncertainty rather than settled pricing.A print that confirms the hawkish case removes that uncertainty. Markets frequently price ambiguity more harshly than a known outcome, and Bitcoin's drop to $76,046 in the hours before the release suggests a market positioned for something worse than what arrived.Positioning supports that reading. The aggregated long/short accounts ratio stood at 1.114, with longs at 52.67% against shorts at 47.29% — close to balanced, with funding subdued at 0.0036%. A market that evenly positioned faces little forced selling into a print, which leaves room for short covering on any reversal.The $76,046 Low Was a Failed BreakdownThe technical sequence is the more concrete signal.Bitfinex analysts had identified $77,100 to $80,000 as the zone where spot demand was absorbing overhead supply — the range in which a squeeze ran into a defined population of sellers.Bitcoin traded below that floor at $76,046 and reclaimed it within the same session. A level that breaks and is immediately recovered tends to strengthen rather than weaken, because the break trapped sellers who now sit underwater.At $79,301, Bitcoin is back inside the absorption zone and roughly $700 below its upper boundary.The Supply Wall Sits Directly AboveThe obstacle above is unchanged by the rebound.Glassnode data shows nearly 8% of Bitcoin's supply was acquired between $80,000 and $82,000 — the largest concentration at any comparable range — with the US spot ETF cohort's average cost basis in the same band and the 50-week moving average at $81,081.Bitcoin reached $82,284 last week before the pullback, and the golden cross confirmed Tuesday after a run from $62,000. Four prior crossovers since 2021 produced the same pattern: the bulk of the rally before the signal, a pullback after it.Clearing $80,000 to $82,000 requires absorbing the densest supply in the market. A 2.68% daily gain does not accomplish that.The Demand Data Has Not TurnedThe rebound does not yet show up in the underlying flows.CryptoQuant's spot demand metric reversed to −145,000 BTC after nearly turning positive at −5,000 in late August. The Coinbase premium index fell to −0.036, indicating US institutional buyers paying below the global market. Crypto ETFs saw $308 million of net outflows Thursday, the worst single day in two months.Those are measured with a lag and will not reflect Friday's session. But a price rebound on short covering and resolved uncertainty is a different thing from returning spot demand, and the two should not be conflated.Two Events Land Before Markets Reopen FullySpot Bitcoin ETF trading pauses once US markets close and does not resume until Monday, leaving the weekend to absorb any escalation with materially thinner liquidity.Brent crude climbed as high as $109 this week after Saudi Arabia told OPEC its crude production fell to 6.238 million barrels per day, the lowest since 1990. US Central Command destroyed five Iranian tankers, Tehran struck American bases in Jordan, and Iran has signalled a restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz.The Clarity Act cloture vote falls September 15. The Fed decides September 16 at 2:00 p.m. ET with updated projections and a Warsh press conference.

data.title: Metaplanet Cuts Executive Reward Pool By 41.1% After Shareholder Pressure
data.description:
Metaplanet cancelled 131 million shares tied to its executive reward pool on Friday, cutting the disputed insider stake by 41.1% after weeks of shareholder pressure. The Tokyo-listed Bitcoin treasury company also scrapped a planned executive incentive vehicle and pushed surviving warrants years further out before they can be exercised, according to BeInCrypto, with unvested awards now unlocking in equal thirds across 2029, 2030 and 2031.

The board reduced each warrant’s conversion ratio to 410 shares from 696 and said the move lifts Bitcoin per fully diluted share by about 8.8%.

data.title: Bridgewater CIO Warns AI May Not Be Regulated Until It Kills Someone
data.description:
Bridgewater managing chief investment officer Greg Jensen warned that AI may not face meaningful regulation until it kills someone, and said the issue should be addressed well before that point. According to BeInCrypto, Jensen made the remarks on Bloomberg’s Odd Lots podcast and compared the current AI mood to February 2020 before COVID-19 reached the U.S.

He cited recent safety incidents involving OpenAI and Anthropic, and said he sees a major AI-driven financial incident or a physical disaster within the next two years without regulation.

data.title: STOCKS | Kroger Cuts Sales Outlook as Oracle Rises on Cloud Revenue
data.description:
Kroger trimmed its annual sales guidance amid fierce competition for grocery spending, while Oracle shares rose after the software company reported better-than-expected cloud revenue on strong AI demand, according to Bloomberg.

Restoration Hardware shares also moved after the home furnishings retailer posted quarterly earnings that beat estimates in a weaker housing market and consumer spending environment.

data.title: STOCKS | TD Securities sees Fed starting rate-hike cycle in September
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, TD Securities strategists said on Friday that they expect the Federal Reserve to begin the first of three rate hikes in this cycle in September, after previously forecasting that the central bank would stay on hold for the rest of 2026. Including Oscar Munoz and Gennadiy Goldberg, the strategists wrote in a Friday note that they expect three hikes in total, with the next two in October and January next year, and said the Fed may not provide forward guidance while the dot plot should be more hawkish. The shift in expectations came after U.S. August CPI released on Friday came in above expectations, prompting traders to raise bets on near-term Fed rate hikes.

data.title: TD Securities Revises September Fed Rate Outlook to Hike
data.description: According to Jin10, TD Securities changed its September Federal Reserve rate outlook from no change to a rate hike.

data.title: Stocks | Optical Communication Stocks Rally Over 3% as the Photonics Trade Reasserts Itself
data.description: Optical communication stocks performed strongly in early US trading Friday, according to BIT market data.AXT led at 3.89%, followed by Marvell Technology at 3.75%, Ciena at 3.69%, Applied Optoelectronics at 3.67% and Coherent at 3.56%. Nokia gained 2.50%, Fabrinet 2.30% and Lumentum Holdings 1.51%. The Pure Photonics ETF rose 2.82%.The Sector Moved Against the Macro TapeThe timing is what makes the move notable rather than routine.Core CPI came in at 0.3% against 0.2% expected, the one figure in the release that missed forecasts and the reading that removes the last argument against a Fed hike next week. The 10-year Treasury yield sat near 4.94% and the two-year at 4.50%, nearly 100 basis points above the fed funds target.Rising discount rates compress long-duration equity valuations most severely, and optical infrastructure names carry cash flows weighted years forward. A sector gaining 3% or more into that backdrop is trading on something specific to it.Marvell's reversal illustrates the shift directly. It fell 0.81% in Thursday's pre-market session, the widest decliner among AI-concept names. It is now the second-strongest performer in this group.The China Supply Ban Is the Live CatalystThe Trump administration has proposed banning Chinese-made optical content and transceivers.Crux Capital's Gaetano, who has covered the sector for over a year, described the market logic plainly on Binance Square's TradFi Essentials: "If the US really wants to ban a bunch of Chinese supply, that is really bullish for non-Chinese supply, especially like the US-based companies."China's position in the supply chain is concentrated at the foundational layer. Indium phosphide substrates — the wafer material most downstream optical content is built from — are produced by roughly three companies holding 80% market share, with seven filling out the rest."A good amount of it is in China, and China restricts the permits of shipping out these indium phosphide substrates to the rest of the world," Gaetano said. "So China kind of controls this bottleneck a bit."AXT's 3.89% gain, the largest in the group, is consistent with that framing. The company produces compound semiconductor substrates, placing it at precisely the layer the proposed restrictions would reprice.Capacity Cannot Respond QuicklyThe supply constraint is not resolvable with capital alone, which is why restrictions on one source carry disproportionate weight.Gaetano summarised the current earnings season: "Almost all the companies were saying, if we can make more, we could ship more. Our customers want more and more of our content, we just can't make it fast enough."Expanding substrate capacity requires qualifying new processes, which takes years. "You can't just throw money at it and overnight just be able to make much more of it."The next layer down faces the same problem. Companies converting wafers into laser chips lack sufficient fabrication facilities, meaning every step is constrained simultaneously.His description of the resulting demand profile: "Before I even make a building to create these materials, somebody's already buying the materials." Capacity scheduled to come online in 2028 is already reserved.Copper Is Losing Ground Every MeterThe structural driver beneath the trade is a physical limit inside data centers.Copper works reliably to roughly two or three meters, extendable toward seven with engineering. As speeds and bandwidth rise, that distance shrinks."Every meter shorter is more optical content that needs to be built out," Gaetano said.Optics began at the longest distances — subsea cables between continents — and has moved progressively inward. The next major step is optics operating within a single rack.The speed progression driving it runs from 400 gigabits per second to 800 and then to 1.6 terabits, with each step lifting supplier revenue through better pricing and more content per system.Two Bear Cases Remain LiveThe sector carries identifiable risks that a strong session does not resolve.The first is hyperscaler capital expenditure and its return on investment. "The entire AI trade is dependent on these hyperscalers increasing their capital expenditure," Gaetano said. "But there's another layer — does the market believe that it's sustainable and can they make it worth their investment?"Many of these companies are pricing substantial growth in 2027 through 2029. Reduced visibility on customer spending into those years would compress multiples regardless of current orders.The second is architecture timing. Co-packaged optics unlocks a market that does not currently exist, and its arrival date is load-bearing for valuations. Delays from integration difficulty — or engineering that extends copper's usable range at higher speeds — would force a rerating.That has already happened in cycles through the year, with CPO delay news knocking the stocks before the market digested it.The Crypto Read-Through Runs Through NeocloudsFor crypto, the relevant channel is the miner-to-AI-compute cohort, and the optical rally cuts both ways for them.IREN holds $2.8 billion in contracts across Microsoft, Nvidia, Perplexity and Figure AI. Hut 8 has its Beacon Point lease. HIVE signed a $350 million GPU cloud deal lifting contracted annual recurring revenue to roughly $180 million.Rising optical component prices raise their buildout costs. Nvidia has already guided third-quarter gross margin to 74% from 75% citing memory, power, land and infrastructure, with a first-quarter price increase planned. Copper set a record above $6.80 per pound, another direct data center input.Those miners lagged badly through Bitcoin's recent rally — the median gain across the top 10 mining stocks was 1.8% against Bitcoin's 22%, with Core Scientific and TeraWulf trailing by 27% and 24%. Cipher Mining fell 6% and TeraWulf 3% on Wednesday as AI infrastructure names gave back gains.Bitcoin traded around $77,000 after the CPI print, roughly 6% below last week's $82,284 high.

data.title: Astemo To Invest $379 Million In Two U.S. Plants
data.description: According to Nikkei Asia, Japanese automotive parts supplier Astemo plans to invest a total of $379 million in two U.S. plants to expand production capacity for electric motors, mainly for hybrid vehicles. The company is moving to lift output as North American demand rises.

data.title: AI Hedge Fund Situational Awareness Active in Options Market, CNBC's David Faber Says
data.description:
CNBC's David Faber said on a live program, citing unnamed sources, that AI hedge fund Situational Awareness has been active in the options market. According to PANews, Faber said Leopold Aschenbrenner resumed buying options in late last week and early this week, paying hundreds of millions of dollars in option premiums.

Faber said the underlying names included companies that have appeared in Aschenbrenner's previous portfolio, such as SK Hynix, SanDisk, Advanced Micro, Bloom Energy, and CoreWeave. He also said it was unclear whether Aschenbrenner had raised new capital for public market investments.

data.title: PitchBook Says ASML Could Reach $1 Trillion Valuation Between 2028 and 2031
data.description: According to CNBC, PitchBook said Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASML is the leading European contender to join the $1 trillion valuation club first, with the company potentially reaching that level between 2028 and 2031. PitchBook said ASML's market capitalization was $257.9 billion in 2025, up 2.6 times in 17 months and growing 30.1% annually between June 2020 and June 2026. Nalin Patel, director of EMEA Private Capital Research at PitchBook, said ASML has been on a strong run in recent quarters. The firm said Europe still lacks a $1 trillion company, citing capital markets fragmentation, regulation and a sector mix tilted away from technology as obstacles. It said only four European companies had revenue above $100 billion in the 12 months to Aug. 20, compared with 14 in the global top 20. PitchBook said Arm is ASML's biggest rival for the milestone, while Novo Nordisk and LVMH have both previously been Europe's most valuable company but have since fallen in value.

data.title: STOCKS | SOFR Falls to 3.62% Before U.S. CPI Release
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the secured overnight financing rate (SOFR) was 3.62% on the previous trading day, before the U.S. CPI release on September 10, down from 3.64% the day before, while the effective federal funds rate was 3.63%, unchanged from the prior day.

data.title: U.S. Consumer Sentiment Falls for Second Straight Month as 1-Year Inflation Expectations Rise
data.description: According to Jin10, the preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment index for September in the U.S. came in at 47.8, falling for a second straight month but by less than 4 index points. Democrats and Republicans both declined sharply, while independents were little changed from August. Expectations for personal finances and business conditions over the next year fell sharply, and consumers said fuel price rebounds and rising trade tensions would put more pressure on wallets. Five-year business expectations were steady but remained well below the historical average, suggesting consumers did not see the new risks that emerged this month as further worsening the long-term outlook. Overall, consumer sentiment was 16% below the level before the Iran conflict began in February and 13% below a year earlier. One-year inflation expectations jumped to 4.6% from 4.0% in August, the highest reading since June, while long-term inflation expectations edged up to 3.4% after holding at 3.3% for three straight months.

data.title: China Sets 2030 Deadline For Mass Self-Driving Vehicle Rollout
data.description: China set a 2030 deadline for the mass rollout of self-driving vehicles, giving automakers a state-backed timeline as Beijing pushes autonomous driving, safety and standards. According to BeInCrypto, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology published the plan on Friday with eight other departments, covering the country’s next five-year economic cycle. By 2030, vehicles with autonomous driving functions should see large-scale use, while highly automated systems are expected to handle expressways, urban express roads and selected city streets.

data.title: Joanne Hsu Says Views on Trump Administration Economic Policy Worsened About 10%
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey director Joanne Hsu said in a statement that views on the Trump administration's economic policy worsened by about 10% this month and remained far below the level in February 2026, on the eve of the Iran conflict, while even Republicans who usually support the current administration's economic policy saw a notable decline in favorability.
